formulations.label: Oral suspension
formulations.strengths: One UK SmPC: dried aluminium hydroxide 44 mg and magnesium hydroxide 39 mg per ml. Another UK SmPC: aluminium hydroxide 175 mg, magnesium hydroxide 200 mg and simeticone 25 mg per 5 ml.
formulations.note: Clinic product: aluminium hydroxide 405 mg + magnesium hydroxide 100 mg per 5 ml. No UK product of this strength was found. This entry uses two UK SmPCs: an aluminium hydroxide/magnesium hydroxide suspension of a different strength, and one that also contains simeticone. Statements from the simeticone-containing SmPC are labelled. Volumes in the dosing section are for the UK products, not the clinic product.

src.q: Each ml contains 44 mg dried aluminium hydroxide and 39 mg magnesium hydroxide.

items.t: Antacid for gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis, heartburn and gastric hyperacidity; indigestion; heartburn and dyspepsia from gastric reflux (hiatus hernia, reflux oesophagitis).

src.q: Antacid therapy in gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis, heartburn, gastric hyperacidity.
Relief of symptoms of heartburn and dyspepsia associated with gastric reflux in hiatus hernia, reflux oesophagitis and similar conditions.

items.t: Simeticone-containing SmPC: symptomatic relief of dyspepsia, heartburn and flatulence.

src.q: The symptomatic relief of: 1. Dyspepsia. 2. Heartburn. 3. Flatulence.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restrictions stated in the two UK SmPCs checked.

items.t: 10-20 ml three times daily, 20 minutes to 1 hour after meals, and at bedtime or as required (UK product with 44 mg + 39 mg per ml).

items.t: Renal impairment: plasma aluminium and magnesium rise; long-term high doses may cause encephalopathy, dementia, microcytic anaemia or worsen dialysis-induced osteomalacia. Prolonged antacid use in renal failure should be avoided (simeticone-containing SmPC).

src.q: In patients with renal impairment, plasma levels of both aluminium and magnesium increase.
a long-term exposure to high doses of aluminium and magnesium salts may lead to encephalopathy, dementia, microcytic anemiaor worsen dialysis-induced osteomalacia
The prolonged use of antacids in patients with renal failure should be avoided.

items.t: Large doses may trigger or worsen intestinal obstruction and ileus in people at higher risk, such as renal impairment or the elderly (simeticone-containing SmPC).

src.q: large doses of this product may trigger or aggravate intestinal obstruction and ileus in patients at higher risk such as those with renal impairment, or the elderly.

items.t: Phosphate depletion (with bone resorption, hypercalciuria and osteomalacia risk) with excessive doses, long-term use, or normal doses on a low-phosphorus diet. Medical advice is recommended for long-term use or if at risk of phosphate depletion (simeticone-containing SmPC).

src.q: or even normal doses in patients with low-phosphorous diets, may lead to phosphate depletion
Medical advice is recommended in case of long-term use or in patients at risk of phosphate depletion.

items.t: Porphyria with haemodialysis: aluminium hydroxide may be unsafe (simeticone-containing SmPC).

src.q: Aluminium hydroxide may be unsafe in patients with porphyria undergoing hemodialysis.

items.t: Hereditary fructose intolerance: should not be taken (contains sorbitol).

src.q: Patients with hereditary fructose intolerance (HFI) should not take/be given this medicinal product.
Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance should not take this medicine.

items.t: Sodium: one UK SmPC states less than 1 mmol (23 mg) sodium per ml, essentially sodium-free. Contains parahydroxybenzoates, which may cause allergic reactions (possibly delayed).

items.t: Tetracyclines and vitamins: antacids inhibit absorption; do not take at the same time (one UK SmPC; the simeticone-containing SmPC also names tetracyclines and vitamins).

src.q: Antacids inhibit the absorption of tetracyclines and vitamins and should not be taken concomitantly.
should not be concomitantly administered with tetracycline-containing antibiotics or any tetracycline salts
tetracyclines, and vitamins

items.t: Any oral medicine: do not take within 1 hour of the antacid; as a precaution separate by at least 2 hours (4 hours for fluoroquinolones) (simeticone-containing SmPC).

src.q: should not be taken simultaneously with other medicines as they may interfere with their absorption if taken within 1 hour
As a precaution, staggering the administration times of any orally administered drug and the antacid by at least 2 hours (4 hours for the fluoroquinolones).

items.t: Named medicines whose absorption aluminium-containing antacids may reduce include atenolol, propranolol, ciprofloxacin and other fluoroquinolones, dexamethasone and other glucocorticoids, hydroxychloroquine, iron salts, levothyroxine, lincosamides, rosuvastatin and tetracyclines (simeticone-containing SmPC).

src.q: Aluminium-containing antacids may prevent the proper absorption of drugs notably H2 antagonists, atenolol

items.t: Levothyroxine may also bind to simeticone, delaying or reducing its absorption (simeticone-containing product).

src.q: Levothyroxine may also bind to simeticone which may delay or reduce the absorption of levothyroxine.

items.t: Salicylates: urine alkalinisation from magnesium hydroxide can increase salicylate excretion.

src.q: Urine alkalinisation secondary to administration of magnesium hydroxide may modify excretion of some drugs; thus, increased excretion of salicylates has been seen.

items.t: Citrates: aluminium hydroxide with citrates may raise aluminium levels, especially in renal impairment (simeticone-containing SmPC).

src.q: Aluminium hydroxide and citrates may result in increased aluminium levels, especially in patients with renal impairment.

items.t: Kidney failure: should not be used (contraindicated in both UK SmPCs). No eGFR/CrCl threshold given.

src.q: Should not be used in patients who are severely debilitated or suffering from kidney failure.

items.t: Renal impairment: aluminium and magnesium levels rise; avoid prolonged use in renal failure. Very rare hypermagnesaemia after prolonged magnesium hydroxide in renal impairment.

src.q: In patients with renal impairment, plasma levels of both aluminium and magnesium increase.
The prolonged use of antacids in patients with renal failure should be avoided.
Observed after prolonged administration of magnesium hydroxide to patients with renal impairment.

hepatic.note: No hepatic impairment statements in the two UK SmPCs checked.

items.t: One UK SmPC: no clinical data in pregnancy; animal studies show no harm; use with caution in pregnant women.

src.q: For Mucogel no clinical data on exposed pregnancies are available.
Caution should be exercised when prescribing to pregnant women.

items.t: Simeticone-containing SmPC: safety not established; use only if the benefit to the mother outweighs the risks, including to the fetus.

src.q: should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefits to the mother outweigh the potential risks

items.t: SPS: aluminium hydroxide and magnesium salts (including magnesium hydroxide) can be used during breastfeeding; no specific infant monitoring is usually needed.

src.q: Aluminium hydroxide can be used during breastfeeding.
Magnesium salts (magnesium carbonate, magnesium hydroxide, magnesium trisilicate) can be used during breastfeeding.
No specific infant monitoring is usually required.

items.t: Simeticone-containing SmPC: maternal systemic exposure is negligible, so no effect on the breastfed infant is expected.

src.q: No effect on the breastfed newborn/infant are anticipated since the systemic exposure of the breast-feeding woman to aluminium hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide and simeticone is negligible.

reproductive.note: No fertility or contraception statements in the two UK SmPCs checked.

adverseCommon.note: Neither UK SmPC lists common or very common adverse effects. Gastrointestinal effects (diarrhoea or constipation) are listed as uncommon.

items.t: Hypersensitivity reactions including angioedema and anaphylactic reactions (frequency not known; simeticone-containing SmPC).

src.q: hypersensitivity reactions, such as pruritus, urticaria, angioedema and anaphylactic reactions

items.t: Hypermagnesaemia (very rare, mainly with prolonged use in renal impairment); hyperaluminaemia and hypophosphataemia (frequency not known).
